problem: Streaming VLA navigation agents such as StreamVLN use only 2D semantic features (SigLIP) and have no predictive component. VGGT-based spatial encoders run out of memory on long episodes and give only relative-scale features, while concurrent predictive VLN work supervises in pixel/depth space, which can overfit to textures and illumination.
motivation: Robust long-horizon navigation needs spatial understanding and prediction of how the scene evolves, not just semantics. CUT3R is inherently streaming and gives absolute-scale features, and JEPA-style latent prediction avoids modeling pixel noise. A prediction branch used only in training can improve representations at no inference cost.
key_idea: Fuse SigLIP semantic features with streaming CUT3R absolute-scale spatial features by cross-attention inside a streaming VLA, and add training-only stream query tokens that predict next-step 2D/3D latent features supervised by frozen SigLIP/CUT3R teachers.
insight: Both latent prediction objectives add gains on top of 2D-3D fusion, and combining them is best (R2R SR 46.7 -> 48.7 in the module ablation). The gains concentrate on medium and long horizons (long SR +4.14, SPL +3.64), with none on short episodes. The attention-mask design is critical: the leaky and no-isolation variants drop SR to about 40 (vs 48.7). CUT3R beats InfiniteVGGT in accuracy and latency, and VGGT runs out of memory, which the authors attribute to CUT3R's absolute scale.
method: Streaming VLA formulation: StreamVLN-style alternating observation-action stream with an N=8 sliding-window KV cache plus long-term memory tokens from 8 uniformly sampled keyframes. Outputs 4 atomic actions per step (forward 25cm, turn left/right 15°, STOP).

2D-3D fusion: frozen SigLIP gives semantic features and frozen CUT3R gives streaming absolute-scale spatial features (state token, pose token). Cross-attention with SigLIP as query and CUT3R as key/value produces fused features, which an MLP maps into the LLM space; keyframes use the same pipeline, each condensed to one token.
Stream query tokens: learnable 2D and 3D query tokens (9 each) are appended to the LLM input per turn during training to reverse-query the streaming context and yield next-step embeddings.

Latent decoders: two 2-layer Transformer decoders with 196 learnable mask tokens reconstruct next-step latent token sequences. Loss is cosine distance for 2D and MSE for 3D against frozen SigLIP/CUT3R teachers on the next frame; total loss is L_nav + γ(αL2D + βL3D) with γ=0.01, α=0.25, β=0.75.

Streaming attention mask: queries attend only to their own and earlier turns, queries from different turns are isolated, and 2D and 3D queries are mutually masked. The prediction branch is removed at inference, so runtime is about 4 Hz with no added latency.
Two-stage training: Stage 1 SFT on R2R/RxR/EnvDrop (~479K). Stage 2 adds DAgger (~260K), ScaleVLN (~314K), and VQA data (LLaVA-Video-178K, ScanQA), for ~938K samples in total.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B (Qwen1.5-7B LLM, fine-tuned) with frozen SigLIP and frozen CUT3R encoders
setting.training_data: Stage 1: VLN-CE R2R, RxR and R2R-EnvDrop (~479K). Stage 2: R2R/RxR, ~260K DAgger, ~314K ScaleVLN, plus VQA data (LLaVA-Video-178K, ScanQA); ~938K samples, 71% VLN and 29% VQA. Table 1 also mentions MMC4 for the † row. Cost is 560 and ~1900 A800 GPU-hours per epoch.
setting.observation: monocular single-view egocentric RGB (no depth, odometry or panorama)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: FORWARD 25 cm, TURN-LEFT/RIGHT 15°, STOP (4 actions per step)

numbers_note: Ablation tables (one-epoch SFT, R2R val-unseen: SR 48.7, SPL 42.9, OSR 57.6, NE 5.82) and real-robot success counts (Table 6) were not included as benchmark entries.
results: PROSPECT reaches R2R-CE val-unseen SR 52.0/SPL 46.2 (MP3D-only) and SR 58.9/SPL 54.0 with extra data. The strongest baseline, StreamVLN†, gets SR 55.7/SPL 50.9 on R2R. On RxR val-unseen with extra data it gets SR 54.6 vs 52.9 for StreamVLN†, and 52.7 vs 48.6‡ in the MP3D-only setting. On the real robot it beats NaVid and StreamVLN in all six scenes (e.g., office 20/30 vs 12/30).
limitations: Real-robot inference is remote (~4 Hz on a dual-GPU server); onboard inference on an RTX 4070 has lower success.
Training is expensive (~560 and ~1900 A800 GPU-hours per epoch), and the RxR MP3D-only StreamVLN baseline numbers come from a different recipe (MMC4 added).
Gains on short-horizon episodes are negligible and absolute long-horizon success remains low (R2R long SR 24.32); the real-robot test uses only 30 trials per scene.
